sentence: In a room, it moves about three hundred forty meters a second.
claim: Sound travels through room-temperature air at about 343 meters a second.
source_title: OpenStax College Physics 2e, 17.2 Speed of Sound, Frequency, and Wavelength
status: OPEN: a person must open the link and check
note: Read: speed of sound is 331 m/s at 0 C and 343 m/s at 20 C.
derivation: The speed of sound in air at 20 C is about 343 m/s.

sentence: The room is five meters across, so the clap crosses it in about fifteen thousandths of a second. Here, that's fifteen seconds. ... would still take about two and a half minutes to arrive.
claim: Sound crosses a 5-meter room in about 15 thousandths of a second: 15 seconds at 1,000 times slower.
note: DERIVATION (our calculation, run it); no outside source. The kitchen width (5 m) is our assumption.
derivation: 5 m / 343 m/s = 14.6 ms; at 1,000x that is 14.6 s; at 10,000x it is 146 s (2.4 minutes).

sentence: Sound covers about a kilometer in three seconds.
claim: Sound covers about a kilometer in three seconds, so counting the seconds between a flash and its thunder and dividing by three gives the distance in kilometers.
note: DERIVATION (our calculation, run it); no outside source.

sentence: Without air, there would be nothing to push, and no sound at all.
claim: Sound is a pressure wave in air, water or a solid, and cannot travel through empty space.
source_title: OpenStax, University Physics Vol. 1, 17.1 Sound Waves
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED (the builder recalled this; no source text was read this session); a person must open the source and check the number and the wording before posting. Standard physics; in space there is no air to carry a clap.
